nodes.label: MetalRenderer README
MetalRenderer (real-time ray tracer for macOS and Metal)
nodes.rationale: A minimal real-time ray tracer with dynamic lights and GI, built for Apple Silicon and tuned for an M1 Max; everything runs in compute kernels.

nodes.label: Custom ray tracing (two-level BVH traversed in the shaders, default)
nodes.rationale: On an M1 Max, which has no ray-tracing hardware, it is 19-24% faster per frame than Metal's intersector in the stress test and on par in the Cornell room.

nodes.label: Per-frame GPU LBVH for moving instances (Morton codes, bitonic sort, Karras hierarchy, bottom-up boxes)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilding from scratch takes 0.08-0.12 ms for 400-2000 objects; an SAH-built moving tree on the CPU traces only 4-7% faster.

nodes.label: One traversal loop for both BVH levels
nodes.rationale: Nesting the bottom-level loop inside the top-level loop let SIMD lanes in different levels wait on each other; merging them almost halved closest-hit cost (12.97 to 6.73 ms). Before that the custom tracer was 35% slower than Metal.

nodes.label: Lights that stay in place are static instances (Scene.LightMotion)
nodes.rationale: Only an animated light's shape is a moving instance: in the Night market 140 of 17329 instances stay in the per-frame tree, cutting the tree build from 0.29 to 0.07 ms. Static shapes get their own tree because one tree over both cost rays 0.5 ms.

nodes.label: Metal acceleration structures and intersector (hardware ray tracing on M3 and later)
nodes.rationale: On an M4 Max hardware ray tracing wins everywhere: frames are 22-32% shorter in the Cornell room and 51-58% shorter in the stress hall, the reverse of the M1 Max result.

nodes.label: Metal TLAS refit with a full rebuild every 16 frames
nodes.rationale: A refit keeps the tree built for where objects were; with 400 objects moving freely rays got 35% slower over 256 frames of refits. Rebuilding every 16 frames traces as fast as every frame for the refit's median cost.

nodes.label: Virtual geometry (Nanite-style LOD DAG of 128-triangle clusters)
nodes.rationale: The gallery's 17.9M triangles trace as a 0.4M-triangle cut in 40 MB instead of about 1.5 GB at about the same speed.

nodes.label: Nanite cut per instance (error under 1 traced pixel), computed on a background thread
nodes.rationale: One SAH tree per model over the cut, not a tree of clusters: the GPU-driven cluster runtime traces 2x slower because overlapping cluster boxes make rays visit 8.6 nodes instead of 3.8.

nodes.label: Spliced BLAS for big cut changes, replaced by an SAH BLAS in the background (hybrid)
nodes.rationale: Spliced rebuilds take 1-9 ms against 20-150 ms for SAH but trace about 50% slower, so they are published first and refined later.

nodes.label: GPU-driven cluster variant (METALRENDERER_VG_MODE=clusters, page pool and streaming)
Cluster DAG simplification that keeps going (locked group borders, seam-aware collapses)
nodes.rationale: Locking only group borders, sliding seam vertices, a relaxed pass across UV seams and passing stuck groups up a level took the DAG from 883 root groups per model to one 366-triangle root and the cut from 62k clusters to 3.9k.

nodes.label: Texture streaming (sparse heap, GPU mip feedback, 1 GB budget)
nodes.rationale: Texture levels come from the largest UV stretch and a histogram instead of a minimum: UV slivers had asked for 4K mips of small models (600 MB resident instead of 14).

nodes.label: glTF model loading (node hierarchy, metallic-roughness materials, KHR_lights_punctual)
Physically based materials (GGX specular, Smith visibility, Schlick Fresnel)
Reflection pass (one GGX visible-normal ray per pixel, denoised indirect specular)
Light types (sphere, spot, sun, rect, tube, emissive mesh)
nodes.rationale: Pipelines are specialised by a Metal function constant for the scene's set of light types, so a scene with only sphere lights compiles to the old code and runs at the old speed.

nodes.label: Shared light helpers: five questions every light type answers
nodes.rationale: Every kernel goes through the same five helpers, so many-lights picking, reuse, the shadow denoiser and all three GI methods work with any mix of light types.

nodes.label: Emissive meshes as lights (one triangle per pixel, own SVGF signal)
nodes.rationale: They take a separate path because the shadow denoiser needs an exact unshadowed term that a mesh does not have; GI rays ignore their emission so the light is not counted twice.

nodes.label: Grouped light picker (4 colour groups, one shadow ray per group, pick reuse)
nodes.rationale: Shadow rays no longer grow with the light count; picking runs in its own kernel because inside traceKernel, whose register use limits occupancy, the same loop cost 4x as much.

nodes.label: ReSTIR DI for many lights (default above 256 lights)
nodes.rationale: Cost depends on resolution, not light count: 16384 lights cost 17 ms where 4096 cost 53 ms with the grouped picker. Below 256 lights Grouped is sharper because its shadow denoiser filters only visibility, so Auto switches to ReSTIR only above 256.

nodes.label: Light table (Vose alias table by power, 10% uniform mix)
nodes.rationale: Built once per scene; moving and flickering lights change only the target function, never the table. The uniform share keeps a dim light close to a pixel pickable.

nodes.label: Light grid (ReGIR: world-space grid of light reservoirs rebuilt on the GPU every frame)
nodes.rationale: The table knows power, not position. The cell target is orientation-free so a draw stays unbiased; per-candidate cell jitter was essential, without it correlated candidates scored 0.8-1.0 dB below the table.

nodes.label: Light-visibility maps (per-light 128x128 distance maps)
nodes.rationale: Secondary hits look up their shadowing there, so radiance cascades need no shadow rays; off above 256 lights where one map per light is too costly.

nodes.label: Global illumination: three methods (radiance cascades, path traced, ReSTIR GI)
Radiance cascades (default GI: screen-grid probes, intervals growing 4x per cascade)
nodes.rationale: Noise-free with almost free multi-bounce light and no temporal accumulation, so cheapest (2.9 ms) and best in the Cornell room; loses 7 dB to the path tracer in cluttered scenes because probes are interpolated across the edges of many small objects.

nodes.label: Path-traced GI (1 spp diffuse path, next-event estimation, denoised)
nodes.rationale: Its large error in the Cornell room is mostly missing energy: with 2 bounces the image reaches only about 88% of the reference's brightness.

nodes.label: ReSTIR GI (reservoir reuse of the path's first bounce)
nodes.rationale: Most accurate method (42.2 dB Cornell, 36.4 dB stress hall) but 2-3x the cost of radiance cascades, so it is not the default. Reuse lowers flicker, not error, after SVGF; spatial reuse is off by default because it adds no PSNR after the denoiser.

nodes.label: Multi-bounce feedback (last hits add last frame's indirect light or its mean)
nodes.rationale: With 2 bounces alone the image reaches 77-81% of the reference's brightness; on-screen feedback raised scores to 31.4 and 34.3 dB, the off-screen mean to 42.2 and 36.4 dB.

nodes.label: ReSTIR GI quarter budget (one fresh path per 2x2 block per frame)
nodes.rationale: 1.7x cheaper and nearly as good on still frames, but a pixel that loses its history waits up to 4 frames for a fresh path (-5 to -15 dB in motion), so it is off by default.

nodes.label: Shadow denoiser (filters per-light visibility only; history clamp, penumbra-limited passes)
nodes.rationale: Direct light is an exact unshadowed term times a noisy visibility, so only the visibility is filtered and shading is never blurred; the clamp keeps moving shadows from lagging (43.9 dB moving against SVGF's 30.2 dB).

nodes.label: SVGF denoiser (temporal accumulation + variance-guided a-trous filter)
nodes.rationale: SVGF's long history smears moving shadows because motion vectors move surfaces, not shadows; it remains the denoiser for indirect light and ReSTIR radiance.

nodes.label: Upscaling (traced at low resolution with jitter, rebuilt at up to 3x)
Custom upscaler (TAAU, default)
nodes.rationale: About 0.5 ms cheaper per frame than MetalFX and much sharper and steadier on stills. Motion took three measured fixes: Lanczos-3 history resampling, a gentle motion cut with a hard one at depth edges, and motion dilation within about one input pixel. It lacks thin-feature locks, so it flickers 3x as much as MetalFX in busy still scenes.

nodes.label: MetalFX temporal and spatial upscaling
MetalFX denoising scaler (MTLFXTemporalDenoisedScaler, upscaler=denoiser)
nodes.rationale: Stands in for SVGF, the shadow denoiser and the upscaler, but costs 1.0-1.5 ms more than what it replaces and scores 3.4-5.9 dB behind, so it is an option and off by default.

nodes.label: Metal 4 graphics API option (MTL4CommandQueue, argument table, residency set)
nodes.rationale: Frames are bit-identical to Metal 3 and whole-frame GPU time is the same within 0.01 ms, so Metal 4 buys this renderer nothing yet. Mip generation, the denoising scaler and texture streaming still run in a Metal 3 command buffer synchronized through an MTLSharedEvent.

nodes.label: Capability gating (options checked at launch, greyed out or skipped when the GPU can't run them)
Blue-noise sampling (128x128 void-and-cluster tile, golden ratio / R2 shifts)
Volumetric fog and light (froxel grid, single scattering, local fog volumes)
nodes.rationale: Computed in a camera-aligned froxel grid of 8x8 traced pixels by 64 slices so cost is 0.2-1 ms; matches a per-pixel ray-marched reference within 1.5%. Fog does not dim light reaching surfaces and has no multiple scattering.

nodes.label: Sky and clouds (one equal-area sky texture, 1/16 of texels redrawn per frame)
nodes.rationale: The sky is one direction-only texture read by camera, GI, reflection rays and fog, so its cost (0.2-1 ms) does not depend on resolution.

nodes.label: Physically based atmosphere (Rayleigh, Mie, ozone, multiple-scattering table)
Volumetric clouds (Perlin-Worley noise shell, 40 jittered steps per texel)
nodes.rationale: Clouds are lit by the clear sky around them (skyMeanKernel) because using the clouded sky would make clouds dark under their own darkness.

nodes.label: Cloud shadows (256x256 transmittance map applied to every sun visibility test)
nodes.rationale: Every sun visibility test multiplies by it so all paths see the same clouds.

nodes.label: HDR sky images (sun found, cut out and replaced by the sun light)
Render Settings panel
Copy as Env (settings as METALRENDERER_* variables)
METALRENDERER_* environment variables (override strings and plain defaults)
Debug window (frame graph, GPU pass timings, scene, VG, textures, memory, traversal counters)
nodes.rationale: Apple GPUs sample counters only at encoder boundaries, so pass timings give each pass its own fenced encoder; without the fence independent passes overlapped and the sum came to 1.6x the frame time.

nodes.label: Geometry debug views (triangles, clusters, groups, LOD level, triangle size, traversal cost)
Benchmark mode (METALRENDERER_BENCH)
nodes.rationale: Each pass runs in its own command buffer so it can be timed, which serializes the frame; frames render back to back without vsync so the GPU's clock stays steady.

nodes.label: How a frame works (CPU animate, TLAS/LBVH, trace, lights, GI, denoise, composite, upscale)
nodes.rationale: Lighting is stored without albedo so the denoiser can blur it freely.

nodes.label: Radiance cascades overlap the denoiser in one concurrent compute encoder
nodes.rationale: Cascades and the denoiser passes don't depend on each other; small dispatches on M1 leave the GPU partly idle, so running them in lock step saves about 0.2 ms.

nodes.label: Runtime shader compile and hot reload (R), built in the background
Cornell room scene
Stress test hall (up to 2000 moving objects, 16384 moving lights)
nodes.rationale: Merging static objects into one acceleration structure made rays about 25% slower because walls and pillars lose their tight instance boxes, so static objects stay instances.

nodes.label: Night market scene (thousands of bulbs, lanterns, rect lights and neon)
glTF Gallery scene (11 models, 17.9M triangles)
Misty hall scene (built for the fog)
Open valley scene (sky and clouds)
Notes for M1 / M2 Macs (no RT hardware, ray budget is the main cost)
nodes.rationale: The frame is traced at 640x400 and upscaled 3x: about 6.0 ms with path-traced GI against 43 ms for a native 1920x1200 frame.

nodes.label: Where to go next (roadmap)
nodes.rationale: Thin-feature locks for the upscaler, a ReSTIR-aware denoiser (ReBLUR/ReLAX-style), 4-wide BVH nodes, a world-space irradiance cache, cheaper ReSTIR GI, deforming meshes, texture compression, a rasterized G-buffer.
